messages:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding a new HF model variant and hit a weird tokenizer mismatch in chat mode. HF tokenizer preserves zero-width-space (U+200B) in a prefix, Redwood pretokenizer drops it, so token counts and alignment drift during eval runs.

ajordan: ugh. can you paste a minimal example? :face_with_monocle:

maya: sure. original string (has ZWSP between words):
```
hello\u200Bworld
```
HF decode/tokenize: `['hello', '\u200B', 'world']` (counts 3 tokens)
Redwood pretokenize -> `['helloworld']` (counts 1 token)
This makes chat-system/prompt prefix caching miss and shifts all token indices in eval runs.

ben: is this in the HF tokenizer's normalizer step (NFC/NFKC) or the byte-fallback pretokenizer?

maya: looks like HF's normalizer leaves ZWSP as it's a formatting char; HF's pre-tokenization step keeps it as separate token piece. Redwood's pretokenizer currently treats all zero-widths as ignorable and collapses them when mapping spaces for chatfmt optimization.

sam: Have you checked the converted `tokenizer_config.json` produced by the HF->Redwood conversion? sometimes `strip_accents` or `do_normalize` flags are different. Also special_tokens_map might drop placeholders.

maya: yes — config.json preserved `do_normalize: true`, but no explicit handling for zero-width chars. conversion script relied on `byte_fallback: true` and then postprocess collapsed non-visible codepoints.

ben: Quick suggestion: convert explicit ZWSP to a visible placeholder token during conversion (e.g. map \u200B -> `<ZWSP>`) and then revert at decode. That keeps token boundaries stable and is reversible.

ajordan: that works but ugly. any chance we can teach Redwood pretokenizer to preserve ZWSP as whitespace-equivalent so chat prefix cache still matches?

maya: I prototyped two fixes: 1) mark ZWSP as whitespace in pretokenizer_rules so `hello\u200Bworld` -> `['hello', 'world']` with an explicit boundary (counts 2) — consistent with HF; 2) map to `<ZWSP>` special token (counts 3) — consistent but requires new special token across serving.

eval-bot: regression check queued: running eval set `chat_prefix_tests_v2` on current main vs candidate with both fixes.

sam: which is preferable for long-term? preserve-as-whitespace seems least invasive. But need to audit other zero-widths (ZWJ, ZWNJ) and bidi markers.

maya: agreed. also noticed edge interactions with byte-fallback: when a byte-fallback tokenizer is enabled, some sequences with 0x00/0xFF bytes get different splits that combined with ZWSP mapping produce off-by-one tokens. so test matrix: normalizer x byte_fallback x zwsp-rule.

ben: do we have perf/latency impact from preserving them vs mapping to special token?

maya: negligible on tokenization path, but special token increases vocab usage and may affect embedding caching slightly. For canary, preserving-as-whitespace is safer.

ajordan: action items?

maya: 1) I'll push a conversion patch that marks ZWSP/ZWNJ/ZWJ as whitespace in pretokenizer rules and add unit tests. 2) Sam, can you put a canary on dedicated with the patch and run `chat_prefix_tests_v2` and `token-align-quant-check`? 3) Ben, if canary fails, prepare the `<ZWSP>` special token fallback plan.

sam: will do, starting canary now. tagging @eng-runtime for observation.

eval-bot: chat_prefix_tests_v2 results: candidate (preserve-as-whitespace) vs main: token-count diffs 0.01% overall, but 3 prompt cases show alignment fixes. no quality regressions observed in llm-chat-macro benchmarks.

maya: nice. i'll open a PR to conversion script and add a note in the model onboarding checklist about zero-width handling + recommended unit tests.

ben: pls include a short snippet to reproduce in evaluation harness so SRE/bench can replay.

maya: done, PR includes harness snippet and the failing examples. thanks all. :thumbsup:
